From 1593 to 1603, a confederation of Irish lords opposed the Tudor conquest of Ireland during the Nine Years' War. The confederacy was primarily comprised of Irish lords Hugh O'Neill, Hugh Roe O'Donnell, Hugh Maguire, Brian Oge O'Rourke and Fiach McHugh O'Byrne.
The confederacy was initiated by Edmund MacGauran, Catholic Archbishop of Armagh, and primarily led by Irish lords Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, and Hugh Roe O'Donnell, Lord of Tyrconnell. Following the confederacy's defeat in the Siege of Kinsale, the confederacy gradually disbanded and surrendered. Tyrone surrendered on 30 March 1603, which is considered to mark the war's end.
In late 1592, MacGauran returned from Spain with promises that Philip II would support Irish Catholics if prior warfare against English authorities was conducted. O'Donnell and Tyrone soon became heavily involved in anti-government activities. On 8 May 1593 at Enniskillen Castle, a letter was signed by Brian Oge O'Rourke and Hugh Maguire, establishing Tyrone, O'Donnell, Maguire and O'Rourke as the primary lords of the confederacy.
